title: Rapid escalation routing playbook and multi-audience status canvas
author: Ava Martinez
content:
Overview

This playbook defines a fast, deterministic escalation routing layer for incidents that require cross-functional coordination, and a set of status templates mapped to audience lanes (customers, internal engineering, executive stakeholders, and security/legal). It is intended for on-call engineers, bridge operators, SREs, and customer success leads.

Scope
- Applies to incidents impacting: API availability, sustained latency / SLO regressions, data-plane integrity, and model-quality regressions with customer impact.
- Excludes scheduled maintenance (use Maintenance Status SOP) and low-impact alerts that fit the Operational Alert handbook.

Goals
- Reduce time-to-first-action for Sev-1 / Sev-2 to under 5 minutes.
- Provide clear, audience-tailored status messaging within 20 minutes of bridge creation.
- Ensure single-source-of-truth (bridge) and automatic routing to the right escalation lanes.

Key concepts
- Escalation lanes: pre-defined recipient groups (On-call Service Owner, Incident Engineering Pool, Customer Success Triage, Legal & Security standby, Executive Liaison).
- Routing policies: rules that map signals and tags to escalation lanes (signal = SLO breach, error spike, KV cache eviction storm, model-sampling drift).
- Bridge templates: standardized meeting/bridge artifacts pre-populated with incident metadata.
- Audience lanes (status canvas): distinct status message templates for Customers, Internal Eng, Executives, and Security.

Escalation routing matrix (high-level)
| Trigger | Primary lane | Fallback lane | Pager policy | Owner if no ack (10m) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| API 5xx > 1% sustained 5m | On-call Service Owner | Incident Engineering Pool | Pager | Escalate to SRE lead |
| P95 latency > SLO x2 for 10m | On-call Service Owner | Incident Engineering Pool | Pager | Escalate to Platform SWE |
| KV cache evictions > threshold | Incident Engineering Pool | Storage team | Pager + Slack | Escalate to Runtime Lead |
| Model quality regression (regression-detector) | Model Onboarding Oncall | Applied ML | Email + Pager (if customer-facing) | ML Lead |

Routing policy implementation notes
- Signals are tagged at ingestion (kafka topic or alertmanager webhook) with metadata: service, region, model_tag, severity_guess, suspected_component.
- A central routing service (incident-router) evaluates rules and calls PagerDuty / Slack / Email based on lane policies.
- All escalations create a bridge document and populate the status canvas skeleton via API.

Runbook: first 10 minutes (operator checklist)
1) Acknowledge the primary pager (0–2 minutes). Record time in the bridge header.
2) Confirm customer impact using metrics dashboards: request-rate, 5xx, p95, error types (2–5 minutes).
3) If the outage meets Sev-1 or Sev-2 criteria, kick off the standard bridge (use bridge-template: rapid-escalation).
4) Tag the bridge with: severity, suspected-component, affected-regions, customer-facing-flag, and impacted-models.
5) Populate the Customer Status lane (see Status templates) and post first customer-facing note within 20 minutes.
6) Assign primary owner and secondary (backup) in the bridge.
7) Enable data collection hooks: capture request traces, logs slice, model-run inputs, and a copy of the most recent deployment manifest.

Bridge operator responsibilities
- Keep the bridge single-threaded: avoid parallel fragments. Use threads for deep-dive subteams.
- Maintain timeline entries (who did what, exact timestamps).
- Coordinate evidence snapshot uploads to the incident artifact store with labels for later postmortem indexing.
- Execute rollback/hotfix policies only with owner and SRE approval.

Audience-specific status canvas (templates)
- Customer lane (external, plain language):
  - Title: [Company] API Degraded — Region {region} — {short impact summary}
  - Body: "We are investigating increased errors for requests in {region}. Impact: customers may see timeouts or 5xx responses. We have an active incident (INC-{id}) and will post updates at least every 30 minutes. Workaround: retry with exponential backoff; set lower concurrency per client while we stabilize."
  - Tone: transparent, non-technical, action oriented.

- Internal Engineering lane (technical):
  - Title: [INC-{id}] {service} — Bridge open — {severity}
  - Body: include: service dashboards links, alert rules firing, recent deploy hashes, KV cache stats, stack traces, and temporary mitigation steps.
  - Tone: explicit about hypotheses, actions run, and next steps.

- Executive lane (briefing):
  - Title: Service Impact — High level summary (INC-{id})
  - Body: impact summary (customers affected estimate), business impact (percent of traffic), ETA for next update, mitigation in progress, and ask (need exec comms approval / sales outreach).
  - Tone: concise, risk-focused, no technical jargon.

- Security & Legal lane:
  - Title: Potential Data / Compliance Impact — {INC-{id}}
  - Body: short description of suspected scope, data classes at risk, immediate containment actions, and request for legal review.
  - Tone: factual and conservative.

Status cadence and templates
- Initial announcement: within 20 minutes of bridge creation. Use Customer lane template if customers affected.
- Regular updates: every 30 minutes while active, then every 60 minutes as stabilization proceeds.
- Post-incident notification: final status and mitigation summary within 24 hours.

Customer comm templates (examples)
- Initial (20m):
"We've detected elevated errors for requests to Redwood's Text Generation API in {region}. Our engineering team is actively investigating (INC-{id}). We will post an update within 30 minutes. If you need immediate support, contact your CSM or open a support ticket with priority 'Incident'."

- Follow-up (60m):
"Update on INC-{id}: Root cause hypothesis: {brief hypothesis}. Mitigation in progress: {actions}. Partial restoration observed in {region}; customers may see intermittent errors. Next update in 30 minutes."

- Resolution (final):
"INC-{id} resolved at {time}. Impact: {summary of impact and affected customers}. Root cause: {root cause}. Actions taken: {mitigation and long-term fixes planned}. If you experienced data loss or customer-facing regressions, contact support at [support@redwood.ai]."

Escalation decision ladder (who calls the execs / sales / legal)
1) If >5% traffic impacted for >30 minutes -> notify Sales Leadership and CSMs.
2) If PII/exfiltration suspected -> notify Security & Legal immediately (pager) and set confidentiality to restricted.
3) If SLA credit or regulatory report likely -> notify Finance & Legal and prepare remediation plan.

On-call rotations, handoffs and expectations
- Primary on-call model: blended SRE + product-service rotation. Typical cadence is 1 week for primary on-call, with 48h shadowing for new members.
- Handoff checklist (to be filled in the handoff channel):
  - Current open incidents and statuses.
  - Recent deploys (last 24h) and known risky changes.
  - Nightly synthetic job health and anomalies.
  - Any escalations to watch.
- Quiet-window policy: no non-emergency merges within the on-caller's first 24 hours and last 12 hours of a shift.

Game day exercises and drills
- Quarterly scenario: Multi-region latency spike with KV cache evaporation. Objectives: validate routing rules, status canvas timelines, and rollback procedures.
- Annual scenario: Model-quality regression affecting top-tier customers. Objectives: exercise product/machine-learning coordination, customer comms, and regulatory escalation.
- Scoring rubric: time-to-bridge, time-to-first-customer-note, time-to-restore, and postmortem action completion rate.

Post-incident process and template
- Within 48 hours: write a 1,000–1,500 word postmortem with the following sections: Summary, Timeline, Impact, Root Cause Analysis (5 whys), Mitigations (short-term and long-term), Action owners, and Customer communications chronology.
- Postmortem quality gate: at least one cross-functional reviewer from SRE, Product, and Customer Success.
- Action completion tracking: actions are tracked in the incident tracker board with due dates and owners; unresolved actions >90 days require escalation to the CTO for review.

Evidence & SLO artifact checklist
- Metrics and dashboards snapshot URLs (UTC timestamps).
- Alertmanager/Signal ingestion raw payloads.
- Request-level traces for 10 representative requests during the incident window.
- Deployment manifests and model checksum at time of incident.
- Customer impact table (tenant IDs, request volume, percent of traffic).

Rollback and hotfix authorization matrix
| Type | Who can authorize | Required approvals | Communication step |
|---|---:|---|---:|
| Hotfix to config (non-code) | On-call Owner | SRE lead | Post to bridge + changelog |
| Code rollback (service) | Service Owner + SRE lead | Product Director | Notify Exec lane and customers if >10% traffic |
| Model rollback / hotpatch | Model Oncall + Applied ML lead | Security review if data-sensitive | Coordinate with CSMs before large customer-facing change |

Operational KPIs to track (post-incident)
- Mean time to acknowledge (MTTA) for Sev-1: target < 3 minutes.
- Mean time to restore (MTTR) for Sev-1: target < 45 minutes.
- Customer update latency (time to first external message): target < 20 minutes.
- Postmortem completion within 72 hours: target 100% for Sev-1, 75% for Sev-2.

Ownership and contacts (examples)
| Responsibility | Team | Primary contact | Pager |
|---|---:|---|---:|
| Incident bridge ops | SRE | oncall-bridge@redwood.ai | Pager: incident-ops |
| API service owner | Platform | api-owner@redwood.ai | Pager: api-service |
| Model incidents | Applied ML | ml-oncall@redwood.ai | Pager: ml-oncall |

Related runbooks and references
- See: /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/incident-evidence-and-retention-playbook-2025
- See: /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/first-five-minutes-operator-cookbook-and-csr-scripts-2026
- See: Maintenance Status SOP (internal)

Appendices
A. Incident-router rule examples (pseudo-JSON)
  - "if alert.labels.component == 'kv-cache' AND alert.value.evictions > 100000 -> route: incident-engineering-pool"
B. Bridge template fields (minimum): Incident ID, Severity, Affected services, Primary owner, Timeline, Evidence links, Customer impact table.

Document ownership and updates
- Owned by: SRE Incident Response Guild.
- Review cadence: bi-annual or after any Sev-1 where MTTR > target.
- Last reviewed: 2026-03-01 (see reviewers above).
summary: Playbook for deterministic escalation routing, audience-specific status templates, operator checklists, rotation and game-day guidance, and post-incident process tailored for multi-audience communications.
